why: Extracted from app.html at c488612 and compared with main (cbc2b20). Exactly one line differs: `rules = f.armyRules … .concat(detachments().filter(d => d.rule).map(d => ({ r:d.rule, src:d.name })))` became `.concat(detachments().flatMap(d => detRules(d).map(r => ({ r, src:d.name }))))`. detRules(d) is `d && d.rule ? Nothing else in the function changed. Rendered result for The Exiled Legion: Blood Tainted is under To do now in every phase of both turns, and Murdercall is left out (its CHECKLIST entry has no s). Compared with main, exactly one line differs: `f.armyRules.concat(Object.values(f.detachments).map(d => d.rule).filter(Boolean))` became `.flatMap(detRules)`. detRules is a hoisted function declaration in derive.js and reads only its first argument, so flatMap's index and array arguments do no harm. A detachment without a rule gives [], the same as the old filter(Boolean). Nothing else changed. The other derive.js changes on this branch (the any-phase regex for 'At the end of a/each phase', move-enemy 'falls back', the Overwatch same-turn guard, the Feel No Pain 'against …' grant) come from the wt-exiled side and are not in these two functions.

where: the-exiled-legion · Phase checklist (data.js CHECKLIST, rendered snapshot)
why: Checked each line against the texts in data.js, GW's Chaos Daemons Faction Pack and Wahapedia. The data.js texts match the pack word for word. Start of the first battle round: Prey of the Blood God ('At the start of the first battle round, select one enemy unit'), a fixed moment with a choice. Command, Movement, Shooting, Charge and Fight, both turns, To do now: The Shadow of Chaos ('At the start of any phase, if you control at least half of the objective markers … until the end of that phase'), a start-of-phase check made in every phase of both turns; Blood Tainted ('At the end of a phase in which …'), an end-of-phase moment in every phase; Grotesque Regeneration ('At the end of each phase'), an end-of-phase moment in every phase. None of these is an activation or enemy-unit trigger, or a bonus with no moment. Fight, both turns: Relentless Carnage ('At the end of the Fight phase, you can select one enemy unit …') and Blood Throne ('At the start of the Fight phase, select one enemy unit within 18" …') both open with a phase-boundary moment and a choice, not 'when this model is selected to fight' or 'each time it attacks', so they are fixed-moment triggers. Neither says 'your', so both turns is right. Active now in Fight, both turns: Prey of the Blood God's re-roll is for melee attacks against its prey, so Fight phases only. Once per battle: Unholy Vigour ('Once per battle, at the start of any phase') appears as a box only in every phase, with nothing of its 3+ invulnerable save under Active now. End of your opponent's turn: Hunters from the Warp ('At the end of your opponent’s turn … you can remove it'). When unclear: DAEMONIC MANIFESTATION and DAEMONIC TERROR. Their words ('each time that unit makes a battle-shock roll' / 'takes a Battle-shock test') name no phase. Battle-shock rolls come from the Command phase's Battle-shock step (08.03), but this list also forces them in the Charge phase (Skullmaster's Devastating Charge), and Insane Bravery counts as one. A single phase would be a guess, and Tyranids' Synapse (battle-shock only) likewise has no phase. Left out correctly: Murdercall, whose trigger is 'each time an enemy unit … ends a move' (an enemy-unit trigger); Shudderblink ('When a … unit is selected to make an advance move', an activation); Bane of Cowards (an enemy unit Falls Back); Brass Stampede, Devastating Charge and Skullmaster's Fury (each time this unit ends a Charge move); Champion Slayer and Skulls for Khorne (attacks); and the phase-scoped bonuses with no choice (Rage Embodied, Daemon Lord of Khorne, Slaughterthirst, Brazenmaw, Instrument of Chaos, Pack Leader). No wrong placement found. Two display points come from main's code and are not this merge's: Blood Throne's unit line reads 'Rendmaster on Blood Throne' without ×2, although the entry has copies:2 and each Rendmaster picks its own target (unitNames counts unit entries, not copies), and Hunters from the Warp, a Flesh Hounds ability, is shown as '· Karanak', the attached unit's short name.
